Actually FT_REALLOC frees the old block, so pointers into the freed block become dangling → UAF read → crash under ASAN.

Wait but the realloc only happens if `blend_used + size > blend_alloc`. First blend with numBlends = N1 → blend_used = 5*N1, blend_alloc = 5*N1. Second blend with N2 needs 5*N2 more → realloc happens (since blend_used + 5*N2 > blend_alloc). So yes, any two consecutive blends will realloc. And the second blend's operands include results of first blend (which point into freed block) → heap-buffer-overflow READ (or heap UAF read).
